1. The petitioner filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injures sustained by him in the road traffic accident occurred on 13.02.2023.

2. It is the case of the petitioner that, on 13.02.2023 at about 11.00 a.m., within the jurisdiction of Malur Police Station, near Jayamangala lake, Malur - Hosur road when the Petitioner was riding unoffending TVS Access scooter bearing registration No.KA-08-EA-5828 in the left side of the road,
at that time the accused/driver of the offending Maruthi Suzuki Swift Car bearing registration No.DL-9-CAG-3542 drove the same from Malur side in a high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endangering human life and dashed against the hind portion of the unoffending vehicle, as a result the rider/Petitioner fell down on the road and Petitioner/ M.V.C.No.3938/2023 3 SCCH - 7 PW-1 sustained simple injuries on his head, left ears, legs and nose.
Thereafter Petitioner was shifted to Government General Hospital, Malur for treatment and for higher treatment he was shifted to ALTOR Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he was treated as an inpatient.
Thereafter, one Venkateshappa.T. given complaint before the Malur police station.

Accordingly, a case was registered in their Crime No.55/2023 and prepared F.I.R. for the offence punishable under sections 279 and 337 of IPC and submitted to the jurisdictional judicial magistrate and the superior officers and investigation was taken up by the investigating Officer.
Further it is alleged that prior to the alleged accident the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was aged about 48 years and he was doing TV Mechanic work and earning an income of Rs.25,000/- p.m.
Due to the injuries sustained in the alleged accident he became permanently disabled and he is unable to do his work normally as he was doing prior to the occurrence of the alleged accident.

The alleged accident is occurred due to fault and negligence act of the driver of the offending Swift Car bearing registration No.DL-9-CAG-3542 and Respondent No.1 is the RC owner of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said M.V.C.No.3938/2023 4 SCCH - 7 offending vehicle, as such the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to Petitioner.
Hence Petitioner filed the present claim petition for seeking compensation.
3. In response to the notice, the respondent No.1 is placed exparte and the Respondent No.2 has appeared through their counsel and filed their written statement.

4. In the written statement of Respondent No.2, the Insurance Company has admitting that the offending vehicle was duly insured with it and the same is valid on the date of the accident and denying the petition averments in part and contended that the Petitioner has not furnished the particulars of the vehicle including the driving licence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further it is denied having insured the vehicle involved in the accident.
The insurer liability is subjected to validity of the DL, permit and other documents in accordance with law.
Further it is alleged that there is no compliance of provision under Section 134(C), 158 of M.V. Act.
Further it is alleged that the alleged accident is occurred due to negligence and fault of the Petitioner and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The driver of the offending vehicle is not possessing valid DL, FC and effective permit at the time of alleged accident.

As such the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation and in order to obtained compensation the Petitioner has constrained to filed the present claim petition.

Further it is denied that the age, income and occupation of the Petitioner and further the petition is false and frivolous in the eye of law and the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimant is exorbitant and reserves the right u/s.170 of M.V. Act., and the driver of the offending car did not possess the valid and effective driving licence as on the date of occurrence of the accident and violated terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
Hence sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
5. On the basis of above pleadings following Issues were framed.

:: I S S U E S ::
(1) Whether petitioner proves that in this accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of driving of Car bearing registration No.DL-9C-AG-3542 and as a result, he sustained injuries?
(2) Whether the petitioner proves that age and earnings of the petitioner as stated in the claim petition?
M.V.C.No.3938/2023 6 SCCH - 7 (3) Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
from whom?
(4) What order or award?
6. In order to prove the case of petitioner, petitioner got examined himself as PW-1 and got marked Ex.P-1 to P.16 and closed their side.
The respondents are not adduced any evidence nor produced documents or stepped into witnesses box.
7. Heard the arguments of both side.

8. My findings to the above referred Issues are as under;
 Issue No.1 :- In the affirmative  Issue No.2 :- Partly in the affirmative  Issue No.3 :- Partly in the affirmative  Issue No.4 :- As per final order

,
 for the following.......

:REASONS:
9. Issue No.1:-
This petition is filed u/s.166 of M.V.Act  1989 for seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the alleged accident.

The petitioner in the petition has contended that, on 13.02.2023 at about 11.00 a.m., within the jurisdiction M.V.C.No.3938/2023 7 SCCH - 7 of Malur Police Station, near Jayamangala lake, Malur - Hosur road when the Petitioner was riding unoffending TVS Access scooter bearing registration No.KA-08-EA- 5828 in the left side of the road, at that time the accused/driver of the offending Maruthi Suzuki Swift Car bearing registration No.DL-9-CAG-3542 drove the same from Malur side in a high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endangering human life and dashed against the hind portion of the unoffending vehicle, as a result the rider/Petitioner fell down on the road and Petitioner/ PW-1 sustained simple injuries on his head, left ears, legs and nose.
Thereafter Petitioner was shifted to Government General Hospital, Malur for treatment and for higher treatment he was shifted to ALTOR Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he was treated as an inpatient.
It is contended that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The Respondent No.2/Insurance Company admitted the alleged accident and its version is that, slowly accused may be driving and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent.
The alleged accident occurred due to negligent and fault of the rider of the unoffending vehicle and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Further it is alleged that the driver of M.V.C.No.3938/2023 8 SCCH - 7 the offending vehicle is not possessing valid DL, FC and effective permit at the time of alleged accident and violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
As such the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation and in order to obtained compensation the Petitioner has constrained to filed the present claim petition.

Further it is denied that the age,
income and occupation of the Petitioner and the petition is false and frivolous in the eye of law and the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimant is exorbitant and sought for dismissal of the petition.
11. The burden to prove the framed issues lies on the Petitioner.

Hence, in order to prove his case,
the Petitioner himself examined as P.W.1 and he has reiterated the entire petition averments and contentions taken in the course of claim petition in his evidence before this Court and also produced as many as Exs.P.1 to P.16 documents.
Therefore, there is no necessity to repeat those facts again.
I have gone through the documents produced by the PW-1.

Ex.P-1 is the True copy of FIR in Cr.
No.55/2023, Ex.P-2 is the True copy of Complaint dated 16.02.2023, Ex.P.3 is the Spot Mahazar dated 16.02.2023, Ex.P.4 is the Spot Sketch, Ex.P.5 is the Wound Certificate, Ex.P.6 is the Charge M.V.C.No.3938/2023 9 SCCH - 7 Sheet, Ex.P.7 is the Notice issued under Section 133 of MV Act to the owner of the offending vehicle, Ex.P.8 is the Reply to notice given by the owner of the offending vehicle, Ex.P.9 is the Discharge Summary, Ex.P.10 is the OPD Record, Ex.P.11 is the CT Scan report,
Ex.P.12 is the Hospital and Medical Bills, Ex.P.13 is the Medical Prescriptions, Ex.P.14 is the X-ray Film, Ex.P.15 is the Adhar Card and Ex.P.16 is the driving licence.
12. In the cross-examination of PW-1 by Respondent No.2, he has deposed that he was riding the unoffending vehicle by wearing helmet on his head.
Further he has denied that he has not possessing valid driving licence.

Further he has deposed that near Jayamangala lake, Malur - Hosur road when he was riding unoffending vehicle in the left side of the road, at that time the driver of the offending car drove the same from Malur side in a high speed, rash or negligent manner and dashed against the hind portion of the unoffending vehicle, as a result the he has fell down on the road and sustained injuries.

Thereafter he was shifted to Government General Hospital, Malur for treatment and for higher treatment he was shifted to ALTOR Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he was treated as an Venugopal.T vs Puneet Kumar on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125136204/
4 inpatient.
As he was under treatment there is three days delay in filing M.V.C.No.3938/2023 10 SCCH - 7 complaint.
His brother has lodged the complaint and he is not an witness to the alleged accident.
He do not know whether he has undergone surgery therein.
He has taken conservative treatment.
He has denied that he has sustained simple injuries in the alleged accident.
Further he has denied that he has not taken treatment in the alleged Hospital in relating to alleged accident.
Further he deposed that he was a TV Mechanic and earning Rs.25,000/- and in this regard he has not produced any documents.
Further he has denied that he has not incurred Rs.1,50,000/- towards his medical expenditure.
Further he has denied that the medical bills of Rs.46,688/- is not related to the alleged accident.

He denied that the offending car is not involved in the alleged accident and in the intention and in collusion with the police and to get compensation they have falsely implicated the offending car and they have filed false case against the driver of the offending car as such the Respondent No.2 Insurance Company is not liable to pay any compensation and he has produced concocted created documents and he is deposing falsely.

During the cross, examination Pw.1 has consistently deposed on the lines of the petition/prosecution case M.V.C.No.3938/2023 11 SCCH - 7 and he has made those versions, which could not be shattered in cross examination.

13. The Respondents contended that the accused is innocent and falsely implicated by the police and the alleged accident occurred due to fault of the rider of the unoffending vehicle and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle and in order to prove its version the Respondents have neither stepped into the witness box nor produced documents and any how the Respondent No.2 cross-examined the PW-1.

14. On careful reading of Ex.P4/IMV report it specifies that the Motor Vehicle Inspector has been clearly opined that, the said incident did not occur because of the mechanical defects in respect of the said offending and unoffending vehicles.
Further the said Inspector noticed the damages to the offending vehicle and opined that, front left side bumper, bonnet, grill and registration number plate sustained damages.

Further the said Inspector noticed the damages to the unoffending vehicle and opined that, front left side body shape scrapped, rear registration number plate, wheel mud guard and silencer damaged and rear left side foot stand damaged.
M.V.C.No.3938/2023 12 SCCH - 7 15.
On going through the Ex.P-5/Wound Certificate it is seen that the Doctor opined that the Petitioner was admitted to the Government Hospital Malur on 13.02.2023.
In the alleged accident the Petitioner has sustained multiple abrasions over the head and bleeding from nose and mild ENT bleed with multiple abrasion.
Further the doctor opined that the said injuries are simple in nature.

16. On going through the Ex.P-2/Statement it is seen that on 13.02.2023 at about 11.00 a.m., within the jurisdiction of Malur Police Station, near Jayamangala lake, Malur - Hosur road when the Petitioner was riding unoffending TVS Access scooter bearing registration No.KA-08-EA-5828 in the left side of the road, at that time the accused/driver of the offending Maruthi Suzuki Swift Car bearing registration No.DL-9-CAG-3542 drove the same from Malur side in a high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endangering human life and dashed against the hind portion of the unoffending vehicle, as a result the rider/Petitioner fell down on the road and Petitioner/ PW-1 Venugopal.T vs Puneet Kumar on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125136204/
5 sustained simple injuries on his head, left ears, legs and nose.

Thereafter Petitioner was shifted to Government General Hospital, Malur for treatment and for higher treatment he was shifted to M.V.C.No.3938/2023 13 SCCH - 7 ALTOR Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he was treated as an inpatient.
The alleged accident occurred due to fault and negligence of the driver of the offending car.

17. On going through the Ex.P3/spot Mahazar it is seen that in pursuance of the alleged Ex.P2/complaint, on 16.02.2023 the police have came to the spot and Sri.T.Venkateshappa showed the spot to the police and the police were conducted the detailed spot mahazar and prepared Spot Sketch in the presence of panch witnesses.
18. Admittedly, the accused is the driver of the offending vehicle and further admitted that,
Petitioner sustained grievous injury due to alleged accident caused by the offending vehicle in question.

The counsel for Respondent No.2 claimed the said Accused/ driver to be innocent and further the counsel for Respondent No.2 contended that, the alleged accident occurred due to no fault of the accused, slowly he may be driving and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent.

19. On going through the prosecution papers, FIR, Spot Mahazar, Spot sketch, MVA Report, Wound Certificate, Charge Sheet, Notice U/sec.133 of IMV Act, reply to the Notice U/sec.133 of IMV Act,
and the evidence of PW-1 M.V.C.No.3938/2023 14 SCCH - 7 is specific to the effect that, the driver of the offending vehicle/accused is the reason for the said incident and at his instance, the incident took place.
The alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.

The evidence of Pw.1 was corroborated to the case of the prosecution and he has supported the manner of occurrence in his evidence in the court and the manner of occurrence is the same as alleged in the Ex.P2/complaint.
It seems that Pw.1 has clearly made those versions, which could not be shattered in cross examination.

Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged by the prosecution, the accused drove the offending vehicle in a rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and at the spot dashed to the unoffending vehicle, as a result rider/Petitioner of the unoffending vehicle sustained grievous injuries in the alleged accident.

The evidence of Pw.1, Ex.P-1/FIR, Ex.P-2/Complaint, Ex.P3/Spot Mahazar, Ex.P4/MVA Report, Ex.P-5/Wound Certificate, Ex.P-6/Charge Sheet M.V.C.No.3938/2023 15 SCCH - 7 clearly establishes that the alleged accident occurred at the spot.
It is not in dispute as to the aspect that, the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the alleged incident.
Because, for the above reasons collectively it is clear that, the accident happened due to rash or negligent act of the accused.
It is evident that injuries noted in the Ex.P5/Wound Certificate would be caused by a road traffic accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused/driver.
Matters being so, the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 279 and 337 of IPC.

Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the injuries of the innocent person/Petitioner aforesaid, as the accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly and negligently on the spot.

Therefore, the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the accused/driver of the offending Venugopal.T vs Puneet Kumar on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125136204/
6 vehicle.
Accordingly I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
20. Issue No.2 and 3:-

The Learned counsel for the Petitioner has contended that the injured Petitioner was aged about 48 years at the time of accident and he is M.V.C.No.3938/2023 16 SCCH - 7 doing TV Mechanic work and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m., and the Petitioner has incurred Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical expenditure.

As such the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head of pain and suffering, mental agony, medical expenses, special diet, conveyance, loss of future income due to disability, loss of amenities and loss of income during laid up period and prays to award the compensation as prayed in the petition.

21. On the other hand the learned counsel for Respondent No.2 insurance company contended that even though the Petitioner claimed that his earning was about Rs.25,000/- per month, the same is not established by the claimant by producing the documents.
Since the Petitioner has not established his income, he is not entitled for compensation towards such prospects and hence prays dismissal of the petition.
22. The petitioner contended that as on the date of the accident he was aged about 48 years and he was doing TV Mechanic work and earning income Rs.25,000/- per month.
The petitioner relied on the Ex.P.15/Adhar Card of the Petitioner and wherein the birth year of the Petitioner is shown as 1976.
Hence it is clear that on the strength of the Ex.P-15/Adhar Card as on the date M.V.C.No.3938/2023 17 SCCH - 7 of the accident the Petitioner was aged about 47 years.
Hence the age of the Petitioner is considered as 47 years.
23. It is not in dispute that the Petitioner sustained injuries in the road traffic accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver/accused.
In the instance case the petitioner claimed that he was doing mechanic work and earning income Rs.25,000/- per month.
But he has not produced any documents to prove the income of the Petitioner.
In the absence of proof of income the notional income as to be assessed.

As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, for the accident taken place in the year 2023, the notional income of the Petitioner taken at Rs.15,250/-.
24.

To prove the percentage of disability sustained by the Petitioner, neither the Petitioner got examined his treated doctor, nor produced disability certificate, hence the Petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head future loss of income on account of permanent disability.

25. As the occupation of the petitioner is considered as TV Mechanic and in the alleged accident the petitioner has M.V.C.No.3938/2023 18 SCCH - 7 sustained multiple abrasions over the head and bleeding from nose and mild ENT bleed with multiple abrasion.
The doctor opined that the said injury is simple in nature.

The injuries shows that definitely the petitioner has suffered pain due to the injuries sustained in the accident, hence an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded towards pain and suffering, mental agony.
26.
The Petitioner contended that, due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he took treatment as an inpatient at ALTOR Hospital from 13.02.2023 to 16.02.2023.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for Venugopal.T vs Puneet Kumar on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125136204/
7 compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- under the head transportation, nourishment and other charges.
27. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has suffered uncomfortable in his day to day life, hence an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities.
28. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the Petitioner would require atleast six months period to recuperate and to get back to his normal day to day activities.
Therefore the Petitioner would be entitled to Rs.91,500/- (Rs.15,750/- p.m, X 6 months) under the head loss of income during laid up period.
The Petitioner has produced Hospital and Medical Bills as per Ex.P.12 for an amount of Rs.46,688/-.
Hence the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.46,688/- under the head of Hospital and medical expenses.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads;
29.

The details of compensation I propose to award are as under:
Sl. Compensation under different Amount in No. heads (Rs) 1 Pain and suffering,
mental agony 1,00,000-00 2 1,00,000-00
Transportation, nourishment and other charges 3 Loss of amenities 1,00,000-00 4 91,500-00 Loss of income during laid up period 5 46,688-00 Hospital and medical expenses Total 4,38,188-00 30.

The Petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.4,38,188/-.
31.
Hence the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fixed on the respondent No.2/Insurance Company and it M.V.C.No.3938/2023 20 SCCH - 7 is directed to deposit the compensation amount.
Thus I conclude that, the Insurance company/Respondent No.2 is directed to the deposit the compensation amount along with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of filing of the claim petition.
Hence, I answer issue No.2 and 3 are partly in the affirmative.
32. Issue No.4:
In view of the findings on the above issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The claim petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.4,38,188/- (Rupees Four Lakhs Thirty Eight Thousand One hundred and Eighty Eight only) with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
Further, Respondent No.2 being insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

Draw the award accordingly.

Matters being so, the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 279 and 337 of IPC.
Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the injuries of the innocent person/Petitioner aforesaid, as the accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly and negligently on the spot.
But he has not produced any documents to prove the income of the Petitioner.
In the absence of proof of income the notional income as to be assessed.
To prove the percentage of disability sustained by the Petitioner, neither the Petitioner got examined his treated doctor, nor produced disability certificate, hence the Petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head future loss of income on account of permanent disability.
